intro_en: A relatively long segment of the Israel National Trail, with desert landscapes and open spaces and the crossing of large streams.
character_en: Comfortable, flat walking on dirt tracks close to the road
transport_en: At the starting point: Tzihor Junction. Along the route: the community of Shittim. At the end point: Shizafon base and Shizafon Junction
pois_en: The community of Shittim. The Great Streams Nature Reserve. Shizafon base. Shizafon Junction
important_en: Near the starting point, about 300 metres west of the point where the Israel National Trail crosses Road 40, there is a designated overnight campsite. There is no water source at the campsite.
The trail passes between active military firing zones; pay attention to warning signs and avoid straying from the marked trail or from the shoulder of Road 40.
Water can be filled at the community of Shittim and at the entrance to Shizafon base.
description_en:
A designated overnight campsite is located about 300 metres west of the point where the Israel National Trail crosses Road 40 (there is no water source at the campsite).
From there, the Israel National Trail heads south on a dirt track that runs south of Road 40. The trail moves away from the road and crosses low hills. The dirt track follows the Eilat-Ashkelon oil pipeline (EAPC), which the Israel National Trail also met in the Makhtesh Ramon and Nahal Hava area (you are invited to read here about the Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel's struggle against the serious environmental dangers of the oil pipeline).
After about an hour's walk, the track approaches the shoulder of Road 40 again. From here to Shizafon Junction, the Israel National Trail runs parallel and close to the road.
The trail crosses the channel of Nahal Hiyyon, while on the left Road 40 passes over the channel on a wide bridge. Nahal Hiyyon is one of the large streams of the Negev. Its two large tributaries, Tznifim and Garzi, are included within a large nature reserve known as the Great Streams Nature Reserve. Nahal Hiyyon begins in the south, on the edge of the Timna Valley, from where it flows north, crossing the Uvda Valley. In this area the stream turns east to its meeting with Nahal HaArava north of Gav HaArava, the highest point in the Arava between the Dead Sea and Eilat, at about 230 metres. From there Nahal HaArava flows north to the Dead Sea.
The Israel National Trail continues south on the dirt track, and the road moves slightly away to the east. A tall antenna and, to its right, treetops on the skyline mark the location of the small community of Shittim, an ashram in the desert defined as a "spiritual guesthouse". Festivals and meditation workshops are held there. At Shittim it is possible to fill water, eat a vegetarian meal and sleep (for a fee) a short distance from the trail.
The trail and the track continue south through monotonous scenery. About 7 km south of Shittim we pass a large military base, Shizafon, the Armoured Corps school.
This is just one of many army bases in the Negev, which are found here in a greater concentration than in any other region of the country. Most of the Negev serves as firing zones used by the ground forces and the air force for training, and by the defence industries for testing. Following the IDF's withdrawal from Sinai as part of the implementation of the peace treaty with Egypt in 1979-1982, the Negev became the main area for IDF deployment and training.
At the same time, 60% of the Negev's area is nature reserves, and half of the reserve area lies within firing zones. Hikers' access to the trails and hiking routes that pass through the firing zones is possible mainly on weekends and holidays, after coordination with the army. The same applies to the marking of the Israel National Trail along its current route in the Negev.
Continuing south, we cross the base's entrance road, and may notice tank training on the other side of Road 40. After a short distance, the trail climbs and crosses a low ridge topped by an antenna. On the other side of the ridge, we descend to Road 12, with Shizafon Junction on the left. Beside the junction is a green patch of trees and vegetation around the roadside inn of Kibbutz Neot Smadar. The kibbutz itself, located east of Road 40, is a true desert oasis.
author_en: Itzik Ben Dov, trail marking coordinator, Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel.
